source.team_first_names: compiled by the shim team from general knowledge of given names common in South and East Asia, Africa, Eastern Europe, the Arab world, Iran, Ireland, Scotland and continental Europe, by two authors writing independently (one list of 255 names and a second of 667 written without sight of any corpus, data file or recognizer), merged; names the sourced first_names hold and Turkish given names (tr_person_names.json) left out; no third-party dataset; a list of names is a set of facts and carries no licence
source.ambiguous_first_names: compiled by the shim team, two authors merged: given names that are also common English or Turkish words, months, days, places, brands or placeholders; plus, derived by scripts/person_names_en.py, the month and weekday names and abbreviations the first-name lists hold, and the Turkish given names (tr_person_names.json) that SSA counts and the Census 1990 lists lack; only entries a first-name key holds; no third-party dataset
source.surnames: US Census 2010 surnames, https://www2.census.gov/topics/genealogy/2010surnames/names.zip (retrieved 2026-10-17, sha256 117c41cb4668727b7627b2845b6df3f83eb2a22a1813f42c0ff4bdcab86de135), Names_2010Census.csv ranks 1 to 50000; capitals written as names, following stopwords and name suffixes left out; public domain (US federal works, 17 U.S.C. 105)
source.following_stopwords: compiled by the shim team: street, place, institution and company words in English and Turkish; no third-party dataset
source.ambiguous_surnames: compiled by the shim team: surnames that are also common English or Turkish words (colours, nature, times, objects, places, function words); derived by scripts/person_names_en.py: entries ranked 1 to 1000 in the Census 2010 list left out (a surname that frequent is a name more often than a word), and the month and weekday names and function words the surnames hold added; only entries the surnames key holds; no third-party dataset
source.not_names: compiled by the shim team from general knowledge: brands, firms, fictional characters, colours and places named after people, matched only as the whole name; names real people also carry (Paul Smith, Tom Ford) are left out; no third-party dataset
source.first_names: US Social Security Administration national baby names, https://www.ssa.gov/oact/babynames/names.zip (retrieved 2026-10-17, sha256 cd78e975ed7bb358e018dd62fbe14ced89295e9581c49172ca4eedcb011b3724): every name with at least 2000 births over all years and both sexes; merged with the US Census 1990 female and male first-name lists, https://www2.census.gov/topics/genealogy/1990surnames/dist.female.first (retrieved 2026-10-17, sha256 bd2f310fc4e5d5e5ea122c9d4342c9821145823118eb20db1647f305ec77b358); https://www2.census.gov/topics/genealogy/1990surnames/dist.male.first (retrieved 2026-10-17, sha256 0a5078ef6effe3b483d15b0f7f95047662126c9bfb624ecd5e5b978fc0f2470b), all entries; capitals written as names, one spelling per name ignoring case and accents, following stopwords and function words left out; public domain (US federal works, 17 U.S.C. 105)
source.function_words: compiled by the shim team: English closed-class words (pronouns, determiners, prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliaries), interjections and short replies, address words, and the Census 1990 list artefact Numbers; never a given name, so left out of first_names, and among the surnames read as words (ambiguous_surnames); Will, May, An and Ever are given names and stay, as ambiguous first names; no third-party dataset
source.name_suffixes: compiled by the shim team: generational and professional suffixes written after a name (Jr., Sr., III, MD, PhD); recognized and left outside the name, and left out of surnames; no third-party dataset
source.particles: compiled by the shim team: lowercase surname particles (van der Berg, da Silva, bin Laden); one or two of them join a name before a listed surname; English data only, since de and da are Turkish clitics; no third-party dataset
